blocks.text: Limits are cgroup settings: exceeding memory gets a process OOM-killed (usually exit 137), exceeding CPU only throttles it.

rows: Soft target under host pressure; no kill

blocks.text:
$ docker inspect -f 'exit={{.State.ExitCode}} oom={{.State.OOMKilled}}' api
$ docker stats --no-stream api

137 = SIGKILL: OOM killer, `docker kill`, or an expired stop grace period. Confirm with `.State.OOMKilled`, host `dmesg`/`journalctl -k`, or an `oom` event. On Docker Desktop, the VM's own memory cap can also be the limit.

items: Each worker loads its own model: 4 workers × 1.2 GB ≈ 5 GB before any request.
`os.cpu_count()` sees host CPUs; set WEB_CONCURRENCY, OMP_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS.
Throttling shows up as latency spikes; check `nr_throttled` in cgroup `cpu.stat`.
tmpfs and page cache count toward memory.

blocks.text: Q: "A container exits with 137. What do you check?" A: "137 means SIGKILL. I check .State.OOMKilled, the host kernel log and docker events for an oom event; if it wasn't OOM, it was docker kill or an expired stop grace period. Then I size the limit from measured peak usage."

items: Size limits from measured peaks plus headroom.
